derivation: For a uniform conductor, the volume between sections is V=S*Delta l. If n is number per volume, the corresponding carrier count is N=n*S*Delta l and its signed charge is q=q0*n*S*Delta l.
For the depicted rightward mean drift v>0 in the chosen rightward-positive convention, Delta t=Delta l/v is positive.
Under the explicitly stated uniform-drift continuum idealization, the signed net transported charge across downstream section 2 during Delta t is q0*n*S*v*Delta t=q0*n*S*Delta l.
Dividing by Delta t gives I=q0*n*v*S. This describes average/net flux, not the individual trajectories of every particle originally between the planes.

For q0>0 and rightward v, I>0. For electrons q0=-e and the same rightward v, I<0; conventional current opposes electron drift. No current arrow or positive-carrier sign is attached to fig-166's velocity arrow.

If drift were leftward relative to the same chosen orientation, the signed v and I would change accordingly and the downstream section would be 1. The source fig-166 depicts only the rightward derivation case; fig-165 separately preserves both conventional-current directions.
The dimensions are consistent: n has inverse-volume units, S area units, Delta l length units and v length/time units, giving I charge/time.

The complete current modern lesson and both full authoritativeText bindings were read. SCI86-1 explicitly says uniform-drift continuous-medium idealization, net charge through section 2, and not every original particle crossing because real particles also have random motion. The modern single dot/arrow is compatible with that clarification and does not depict tracked trajectories of all particles.

The original assembled source text retains its historical every-original-particle wording for provenance. It is not substituted for the corrected modern prose, and the lesson's historical ampere-definition qualification is preserved.

In both actual modern previews, the short arrow is above the outer top contour while v is below that contour inside the conductor. The main drift arrow still points right and the net-flow derivation remains correct; those successes do not make the detached vector notation faithful.
